connector: Last week ended with Lucy coming last, crying. Tonight she wakes alone and hears the voice she likes best in the world. This week, watch the choices that keep coming back. When one choice echoes another, the story is pointing at its big idea.

a.raw: at night lucy crept out of the camp because she herd aslan calling her name in the forrest
a.fixed: At night, Lucy crept out of the camp because she heard Aslan calling her name in the forest.
a.why: Capitals on At, Lucy and Aslan; a comma after the opening phrase At night; heard, not herd; forest has one r; a period ends it.

b.raw: edmund woke first but he could not see aslan in the moonlight
b.fixed: Edmund woke first, but he could not see Aslan in the moonlight.
b.why: Capitals on Edmund and Aslan; a comma before but joins two complete thoughts; a period ends it.

notes.wgrd: Notice theme through repeated choices: mark each choice in a few words, hunt for an earlier choice it echoes, and say the two together.
vocab: A very steep cliff or drop.
A rough camp without proper shelter.
Able to feel and sense things; aware.
notes.wordParts: Latin bases: rupt = break, duct and duce = lead, form = shape: interrupt, conduct, introduce, transform.
notes.grammar: Commas in dates and places: a comma between the day and the year (June 12, 1941), between a town and its county or country (Dover, Kent), and another after them if the sentence goes on.
notes.spelling: Greek and Latin parts you know: port (carry), spect (look), script and scribe (write), rupt (break), tele (far). Spell the part the same way every time: inter + rupt + ion.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: The OAO Seven Pillars are honesty, respect, courtesy, responsibility, courage, service and perseverance. In Chapter 10, Lucy finds Aslan and has to go back for the others. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: Lucy starts to complain that the others wouldn’t believe her. Then she says, “I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to start slanging the others.”
items.why: She stops blaming others and owns what she said.

items.t: Aslan tells Lucy she must wake the others and follow him, even if they don’t believe her. She hides her face in his mane, then sits up: “I’m sorry, Aslan. I’m ready now.”
items.why: She is afraid of being laughed at and goes anyway.

items.t: Lucy has to tell her story to each of them. Each time she says it, it sounds less convincing. She keeps saying it.
items.why: She keeps going when it gets harder each time.
items.hint: What happens each time she says it?

transcripts.welcome: Hello, it’s Nell. Last time, Lucy lost the vote and came last, crying. Tonight she wakes up alone, and someone is calling her name. Today’s question: what does it cost to trust what only you can see?
transcripts.read: Watch for echoes. Has anyone in this book already had to decide whether to believe Lucy? Mark each choice in a few words as you read. And listen closely to what Aslan tells her about what would have happened.
transcripts.morphology: Three more Latin bases. Rupt means break, so to interrupt is to break in. Duct and duce mean lead, so an aqueduct leads water across a valley. Form means shape, so a formation is a shape made by many people. Find the base. It carries the meaning.
